top.title: Hundreds of million for 90 minutes, peanuts for a lifetime of service, by Stephanie Shaakaa
top.description: *Nigeria’s Broken Scale of Value When the Super Falcons clinched their record-extending tenth Women’s Africa Cup of Nations title in July 2025, the Presidency rolled out the red carpet. The players received national honours, three-bedroom apartments in Abuja and the promise of the naira equivalent of $100,000 each. The financial rewards were eventually fulfilled in November 2026. Barely had that celebration settled when another Nigerian women’s team made history. The Flamingos conquered the world, becoming the first African country to win the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. Once again, the presidential purse swung open: ₦100 million for each player, secured in savings certificates because of their young age, ₦100 million in cash for the coach and ₦50 million for each member of the technical crew. The Senate also announced a separate ₦100 million reward. Let us be clear: nobody begrudges these young girls their glory. They trained hard, carried the green-and-white flag with pride and earned their moment in the sun. Their achievement deserves recognition, and the decision to preserve their rewards in savings instruments rather than hand enormous sums directly to teenagers is commendable. The problem is not that the government rewards sporting excellence. It is what the speed, scale and enthusiasm of these announcements reveal about the Nigerian state’s priorities. There is a disturbing arithmetic to our national life: hundreds of millions for 90 minutes of football, and peanuts, sometimes outright silence, for a lifetime of service. See the contrast in Abuja. When a trophy arrives at the Presidential Villa, the government can announce substantial financial commitments, organise receptions and put together carefully structured reward packages. Even the decision to protect the Flamingos’ money through savings certificates demonstrates an ability to think ahead and make financial arrangements in the interest of young beneficiaries. Yet, outside the celebratory atmosphere of the Villa, citizens encounter a different government, one that appears to require endless negotiations, industrial threats and public agitation before certain obligations receive the attention they deserve. The contrast extends beyond workers and pensioners. Consider the survivors of the Yelewata massacre in Benue State. Having lost family members, homes and livelihoods to violence, many displaced residents continue to struggle with food, healthcare, decent shelter and other basic necessities. Investigations into conditions in Benue’s displacement camps have documented irregular food distribution, inadequate sanitation, poor healthcare facilities and families struggling to secure even one proper meal a day. These are Nigerians whose lives have been shattered by violence. They are not asking for presidential honours or millions in savings certificates. top.description: By Bunmi Sofola Here, a marriage counselor who has spent 16 years sifting through the ruins of other people’s relationships, gives his analysis of how a partnership can lose its way, and a few suggestions for not letting it happen. (a) Signs she is having an affair Look for a sudden short-term drop-off sex: Everyone has appetites – exactly where is she satisfying hers? Radically different sexual behavior: If she suddenly starts suggesting things he hasn’t done before, or doing things every differently even if it’s better, where is she getting the ideas from? Sudden increase in working hours: This can easily be innocent, but where’s the extra cash? (You might never know if lover boy is giving her over-time pay!) Sexually transmitted infections: Towels and toilet seat explanations simply aren’t good enough. (b) Things she is getting from an affair that she is not getting at home Excitement that is the main thing. Having a secret life. If you are clever enough, your marriage should be her secret life! top.title: ‘Really proud’ – Aaron Rodgers shares rare photo with ‘little bro’ Jordan in relationship update
top.description: Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images Aaron Rodgers’ family circumstances have been a big talking point throughout his career, but the veteran quarterback has been working on fixing those relationships of late. The 42-year-old is playing into the final months of his career in the NFL, as he prepares to hang up his cleats at the end of the current season. The Pittsburgh Steelers are in a good position, but this weekend’s game against the Cincinnati Bengals will tell a lot about where they are. Along the journey of his final season in the league, Rodgers is clearly looking for opportunities to bring his family along on the journey. Taking to his Instagram account, the Steelers’ quarterback has now shared a photo of himself and his younger brother, Jordan, in a rare sighting of the two together. Aaron Rodgers admits he’s ‘proud’ of younger brother Jordan in rare sighting together Rodgers’ younger brother Jordan works for ESPN, and has been working as part of their coverage for this weekend’s upcoming College Football fixtures. On Friday evening, the Acrisure Stadium hosted Pittsburgh vs Florida State. With Jordan working for ESPN’s coverage at the home of the Steelers, it provided Aaron with the perfect opportunity to catch up with his younger brother. Taking to Instagram, Rodgers said: “Great to see little bro @jrodgers11 in his element tonight @acrisurestadium. Really proud of how hard he’s worked to get to where he is now 👊🏻.” The photo shared showed the pair smiling from ear to ear, with fans in the comments sharing their delight at seeing the two brothers together. Their relationship has been strained over the years, with Jordan admitting as much on television shows in the past. However, this marks a real step forward in patching up their relationship, with Rodgers seemingly looking for a settled life as he prepares to call it a day on his career. Jordan Rodgers praised Aaron recently on ESPN for his skills at quarterback, but he will certainly cherish his improved relationship with his brother over what he is able to do on a football field. top.title: Grady Hirst-led West Branch football upsets Rocky River in OHSAA playoffs
top.description: ROCKY RIVER — Grady Hirst ran for two touchdowns in the final 5:37 as West Branch (11-1) rallied for an impressive 21-12 win over previously unbeaten Rocky River (11-1) in a Division IV, Region 13 semifinal on the road. Hirst gave West Branch the lead with a 2-yard touchdown with 5:37 to play and then sealed the win with another 2-yard TD run with just 3:27 left. Hirst ran for 203 yards and all three West Branch touchdowns on 36 carries. The Youngstown State recruit was 11-of-18 passing for 84 yards with no interceptions. Gavin Marshall put an exclamation point on the victory with an interception on Rocky River's final drive that allowed West Branch to take a knee to run out the clock and advance. Jeremy Ramsey also intercepted a pass for West Branch. Marshall led West Branch in receiving with five catches for 54 yards. Watch Ohio High School Football Live on NFHS Network all year Rocky River scored two first-quarter touchdowns but was shut out the rest of the game. Carter Atwater threw a touchdown and ran for a touchdown for the Pirates. Rocky River missed an extra point after its first touchdown and failed to convert a 2-point conversion pass on its second touchdown. That allowed West Branch to take a 14-12 lead with 5:32 remaining in the fourth quarter after Hirst scored on a 2-yard run. Rocky River was limited to just seven first downs and 173 yards of total offense. Kentucky recruit Tristin Hughes was held to 44 yards receiving on three catches for Rocky River. Rocco Baon was the top offensive performer for the Pirates with 50 yards rushing on 16 carries. West Branch got two pass deflections on defense from Landon Coffee. Coffee also caught a key 2-point conversion from Hirst with 3:27 left to extend the West Branch lead to nine points and make it a two-possession game. West Branch advances to the Division IV, Region 13 championship game against No. 5-seeded West Geauga (11-2) on Friday, Nov. 20. The game will be played at a site to be determined. top.title: Villarreal forward opens door to Barcelona move with admission about childhood dream: ‘Club of my heart’
top.description: Villarreal forward opens door to Barcelona move with admission about childhood dream: ‘Club of my heart’ Villarreal striker Georges Mikautadze has admitted that Barcelona have been the club of his heart since childhood, describing the Catalan side’s interest in him as flattering while expressing his ambition to earn a move to one of Europe’s biggest clubs. In an interview with DAZN , the Georgia international discussed Barcelona’s previous interest and made it clear that the speculation has provided additional motivation. His comments are particularly interesting given that Barcelona considered him as a potential attacking reinforcement during the summer of 2026, when the club was assessing options for the future of Robert Lewandowski. Mikautadze admits Barcelona have been his dream club Discussing the links with Barcelona, Mikautadze admitted that he is a lifelong Barcelona fan and it makes him happy that they were interested in him. Georges Mikautadze admits he is a Barcelona fan. (Photo by Stu Forster/Getty Images) “Barcelona has been the club of my heart since I was a kid. It’s flattering to hear about their interest. “I still watch the Barcelona games… But it’s up to me to work hard and earn the chance to move to a big club like Barcelona,” he revealed. It is crucial to remember that the Georgian forward has previously explained that his admiration developed during the era of Xavi, Andres Iniesta, Sergio Busquets and the famous attacking partnership known as MSN. “Barcelona’s interest? Yes, it’s flattering and gives me even more motivation. It also means I’m doing a good job. Georges Mikautadze is ready to take the next big step in his career. (Photo by Stu Forster/Getty Images) “Besides, when I was young, I was a Barcelona fan, ever since the days of Xavi, Iniesta, Busquets and MSN. But I hadn’t really thought much about it,” he had said. Barcelona faced financial obstacles despite Mikautadze’s interest Meanwhile, Mikautadze also talked about his readiness to take the next step in his career, despite recognising that he still has room to improve. “I’ve turned 26, but I think I’m ready to move to a big club. I have everything it takes, and I try to show that every time. Maybe I just need a little more time,” he said. However, it must be remembered that Villarreal are in a strong negotiating position, as his release clause increased from €60 million to €78 million in August 2026, while his contract also runs until 2031.

top.title: Mauricio Pochettino: why the newly appointed Man United manager will take this star to the stratosphere
top.description: Mauricio Pochettino: why the newly appointed Man United manager will take this star to the stratosphere Manchester United have not made the best signings in recent years. Last summer was seen as an outlier, though, as all four players, Matheus Cunha , Bryan Mbeumo, Benjamin Sesko and Senne Lammens, all played key roles as United went from 15th to third in the league. This season has evidently been a disaster so far, as they sit 18th in the league in November, and Michael Carrick has paid for this start with his job. Matheus Cunha Whilst Cunha has not hit the heights of last season, he has still provided four goals and five assists in all competitions. This included a stunning brace to beat AS Roma in a magical night at Old Trafford in the Champions League earlier this month. Nonetheless, Cunha struggled under Carrick at times, playing as a number nine and being shunted out of his natural position to accommodate Marcus Rashford since his return this season. Mauricio Pochettino will love him Much has been made of incoming Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino’s admiration for Rashford , but he will arguably love Cunha’s profile more. Cunha will fit the Argentine’s tactics like a glove. According to Premier League analysis , Pochettino favours “a 4-2-3-1 system where wide attackers operate as roaming inside forwards rather than rigid touchline wingers. Starting on the left, Cunha can drift centrally into the pockets between midfield and defence while an overlapping full-back.” The Brazil international always looks more dangerous when he has licence to drift in and out and also drop into midfield, so this will be great news for him. In addition, players like Dele Alli and Cole Palmer, who like to operate in the half-spaces, have traditionally done well for Pochettino, so there is no reason to believe Cunha cannot also benefit. The former Tottenham Hotspur coach’s system also heavily relies on high pressing, and United are not a team full of natural pressers. Cunha, however, is great at pressing and harrying defenders into mistakes, and it seems natural that he would adapt well to Pochettino’s demands. What’s more, the head coach also likes to employ fast transitions in attack and, once again, Cunha has often hurt teams in England like this for Wolverhampton Wanderers and United. Finally, the head coach is renowned for his ability to man-manage and forge strong relationships with players. Therefore, he may just be the man to get the occasionally erratic Cunha to click, feel loved and stay on task. Featured image by Justin Setterfield via Getty Images online polls

top.title: Barcelona, Real Madrid, PSG, Milan and Brighton tracking young Brazilian star
top.description: BELO HORIZONTE, BRAZIL - SEPTEMBER 12: Vitao (C) of Atletico Mineiro celebrates with teammates after scoring the team's third goal during the Brasileirao 2026 27th-round match between Atletico Mineiro and Fluminense at Arena MRV on September 12, 2026 in Belo Horizonte, Brazil. (Photo by Pedro Vilela/Getty Images) | Getty Images The two La Liga giants, two other big teams in Europe, and one team from England are among the European clubs after Vitor Fernandes Chaves Teixeira, also known simply as Vitão, according to a new report . An U17 FIFA World Cup champion with Brazil, Vitão has broken through at Atlético Mineiro in his national league, and many clubs in Europe have taken note. A tall center-back who recently scored his first senior level goal, Vitão is said to be tracked by FC Barcelona, Real Madrid, Paris Saint-Germain, AC Milan, and Brighton. The Galo is said to be willing to let him go for £12 million, which would be a significant sale for them. He has a contract until 2028. The Brazilian league is due to end in December, so there is a chance that he goes in the European winter transfer window, though the report notes the club wants to keep him until summer 2027 if possible. Barcelona is on the hunt for new defenders, being somewhat thin in the center-back position due to a combination of injuries, loss of form, and the departure of Iñigo Martínez in the transfer window last year. Still just 18 years old, Vitão may not be fully ready to contribute at elite teams in Europe just yet. But there is a growing feeling that he will be making the jump across the Atlantic to the top five leagues sooner rather than later.

top.description: (Photo by Ian Walton/PA Images via Getty Images) | PA Images via Getty Images Former England manager Roy Hodgson believes Harry Kane has developed into an even more formidable player since his time working with the striker a decade ago, while also expressing his confidence in the depth of the current England squad. Hodgson briefly worked with Kane ahead of EURO 2016, witnessing the early stages of what would become an extraordinary career. Hodgson reflected on just how much the Bayern Munich striker has evo “Harry Kane, of course. We had Harry Kane for a short period of time. We took him in just before the Euros, but that was 10 years ago. So it’s a much better and much stronger Harry Kane than we had with us, but we saw the enormous potential that he had,” Hodgson told The Jeff Stelling Show, produced by OLBG . The former England boss also praised the options avail able to Thomas Tuchel, suggesting the current squad has the depth to compete across every position. “I d on’t see any weaknesses in the England team. I don’t look at it and think, ‘Well, they’re going to struggle here because they don’t have that type of center-half, that type of fullback, that type of central midfielder.’ I see there’s a choice everywhere to fill those positions as I certainly would like to fill them, and I see Thomas Tuchel filling them. top.title: Mirra Andreeva reacts to having to face Jessica Pegula next in the WTA Finals after their hot mic controversy
top.description: As if by some inevitable act of fate, Mirra Andreeva and Jessica Pegula will face one another next in the WTA Finals semi-finals. Their controversy before the tournament began had many scrambling for the fixture list to see if and when they might meet. There were many permutations and potential outcomes, but given how sport often works, the storyline had written itself. Now, not only will we get to see a first-ever meeting between these two elite-level ball-strikers, but we will also get to see how they react after such pre-match drama rocked the tennis world. Pegula was heard calling Andreeva a ‘diva’ during a long rant, mistakenly live-streamed to thousands on the WTA’s official YouTube channel. Andreeva has already reacted to Pegula’s comments , indicating they swiftly moved on. Now, she has the chance to prove it. Mirra Andreeva prepares to face Jessica Pegula for the first time in her career Speaking on court after yesterday’s win over her good friend and last-minute call-up Diana Shnaider, the Russian was asked about facing Jessica Pegula , to which she briefly spoke to the Indian Wells crowd. She pleaded, jokingly: “Well, uh, one thing I know for sure, it’s not gonna be an easy match. “Guys, please, I know it’s probably gonna be like 80-20, but maybe, I don’t know, if you could do like 60-40 tomorrow, that would be great!” Then, in a separate interview with the WTA media, Mirra Andreeva expanded on her fine form, having gone 3-0 in her first-ever WTA Finals group stages. Asked how happy she was, the 19-year-old insisted: “Yeah, I am, to this moment, I’m feeling super, super happy with the way I was playing, with the way things went, and it was not an easy last-minute change for me to find out that I’m gonna be playing against Diana, my good friend. top.title: ‘I May Lose My Mind’, Frustrated Travellers React To US Flight Havoc
top.description: Confusion reigned at airports across the United States on Friday as a rare grounding of all US flights stranded hundreds of thousands of frustrated travellers. In New York’s busy LaGuardia airport, Janice Llewellyn was on the verge of tears: the chaos could mean she will miss her daughter’s wedding in Toronto. The 61-year-old Llewellyn was desperate to find an alternative route, telling AFP: “I may lose my mind.” “My husband flew all the way from England to get to the wedding,” she said. “Oh gosh! I wish they had another flight, I wish I could get another flight, like, now.” At the airport in Las Vegas, some fliers were told their journeys were delayed due to wind. One airline staffer said the ground stop would last eight hours. Another said 24 hours. Passengers wait for updates at a check-in area at Terminal 7 at Los Angeles International Airport, in Los Angeles on November 13, 2026. US aviation regulators issued an extremely rare ground stop of all flights across the country on November 13 after a major communications outage, which the Department of Homeland Security said did not appear to be the result of any “nefarious attack.” Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) officials eventually lifted the ground stop at 8:15 pm ET (0115 GMT Saturday). “It will take us time (to) resume normal operations,” Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy said, blaming the incident on telecommunications issues with decades-old equipment. During the stop, the lack of information led many passengers to form long lines at rental car counters in a mad dash for travel alternatives. Joseph Anderson said he was trying to get back to Oakland in California from Las Vegas and was considering driving — but said “if the whole country is stopped, that means the highways are going to be jammed too.” The 72-year-old retired Air Force veteran said his already-checked luggage was captive, meaning “we’re kind of stuck.” “I would hope the communication can be better from the FAA,” he said. Passengers wait in line to retrieve their luggage as flights were cancelled at Chicago O’Hare International Airport in Chicago on November 13, 2026. Friday 13th The ground stop comes less than two weeks before the Thanksgiving holiday, the busiest travel period of the year in the United States. And it falls ahead of a particularly busy weekend for professional and college sports — teams and their fans are also stuck. top.description: As Scotland legend Kenny Dalglish watched one of his records equalled in Scotland's 2-1 win over North Macedonia, another of his feats loomed into view. The night was supposed to be about Andy Robertson joining Dalglish as Scotland's most-capped man, the Tottenham left-back making his 102nd appearance for his country. But instead, for the first time, the 75-year-old might be nervous that his crown as one of Scotland men's all-time top goalscorers is wobbling. That is because, in Scotland's rather humdrum Nations League victory, John McGinn - in his 94th Scotland appearance - took two big strides towards the record. The Aston Villa midfielder now has 24 goals for his country - six shy of Dalglish's long-standing record of 30, shared with Denis Law. "It's something that's been in the back of my head," McGinn admitted in the post-match debrief. "If I start climbing that table, it means we've been successful as a team." Now 32 years old, time is running out for him. But as he pulls level with Hughie Gallacher, one of the Wembley Wizards of folklore, his ambition is clear. McGinn double gives drab Scotland win over North Macedonia The rise and rise of 'Meatball' McGinn McGinn 'definitely capable' of reaching record There was a time when talk of this record being toppled seemed laughable. Scotland has produced strikers in recent decades, but none close to Dalglish or Law. The fact a midfielder might take the title makes McGinn's feat all the more astonishing. His prowess in front of goal is no secret to the Tartan Army. There was the spell at the end of 2019 where he scored six in three games, his overhead kick against Austria, his late winner against Croatia in 2024. But of late, his lack of goals and even his performances have had some fans questioning where he fits into the Scotland team. "It has been a bit of a dry patch for me over the last year on the goal front," McGinn admitted, and he's not wrong. He failed to find the back of the net for Scotland in 2025, the first time he'd done that since 2020. But, just as his form at Villa has sky-rocketed, he came up big for his new international head coach Sebastien Pocognoli. "Isn't it great to have a John McGinn in your team?" former Scotland winger Pat Nevin said on Sportsound. "He's somebody you'd want to have in your team to be taking a penalty for you. "I'd be surprised if John McGinn doesn't get the goal record now. It might take him another year or two, but he is definitely capable of getting that record." 'The best person I've met in football' Becoming Scotland's main penalty taker will help, a fact McGinn alluded to coyly post-match. In his career, he had only taken one spot-kick before this season - scoring for Scotland in the 3-3 draw against Norway back in 2023. top.title: David Warner accuses Cricket Australia of ‘cover up’ over sandpaper scandal
top.description: David Warner has sensationally accused Cricket Australia (CA) of executing a “cover-up” of the “sandpapergate” ball-tampering scandal in 2018. Warner, then vice-captain, was one of three players to serve long bans after a CA investigation into the use of sandpaper on the ball during the Test series against South Africa. Usman Khawaja had reopened the saga by writing in his autobiography that the whole Australian team were aware of the ball tampering, drawing support from close friend Warner and a strong denia l from now-skipper Pat Cummins . Warner, who retired from international cricket in January 2024, has now claimed that Cummins and the rest of the bowling attack – who have always denied wrongdoing – were not interviewed as part of the investigation. David Warner (left), Cameron Bancroft and Steve Smith all served bans for their role in the ball tampering scandal (Reuters) “As far as l am aware, CA did not interview Josh Hazlewood , Mitchell Starc or Nathan Lyon in their 2018 investigation," Warner said in a post on Instagram. "If that's correct, then how can CA push the idea that the bowlers didn't know? "It looks like they had decided who they wanted to blame from the very beginning, ran a shoddy investigation to serve the purpose and now they want to maintain the false narrative that the bowlers had no idea. That stinks of a cover-up." Cummins suggested on Friday that he had been talked to as part of enquiries in 2018. He, Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon have always maintained that they were unaware that sandpaper was brought on to the field in Cape Town to tamper with the ball. Australia captain Pat Cummins spoke to the media for more than an hour as he responded to Usman Khawaja’s claims (Reuters) Warner, captain Steve Smith and batter Cameron Bancfroft were the only players punished by Cricket Australia in 2018. Head coach Darren Lehmann was cleared of wrongdoing, though resigned his role at the end of that series. In response to the former opener’s new claim, a Cricket Australia statement said: “As we have stated previously, all players were given the opportunity to speak at the time of the initial investigation and have had the ability to come forward with new evidence in the eight years since. "Subsequently, CA has respected every player and former players' right to provide their own version of events." CA has previously said that it does not intend to reopen the investigation.

top.title: Trump, Xi, Putin to hold historic meeting in China – White House
top.description: Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping will hold the first ever three-way meeting between the leaders of the United States, Russia and China at a summit in Shenzhen next week, the White House said Friday. Trump wants to talk about reducing nuclear arsenals at the trilateral talks on Thursday and is also set to bring up his war in Iran — but he is not expected to discuss Russia’s war in Ukraine, US officials said. The three leaders will meet on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in the southern Chinese city, White House spokeswoman Olivia Wales told reporters. “The president has made it clear that, among other topics, he will discuss the reduction of nuclear weapons in the world. This proliferation, President Trump believes, is very dangerous,” Wales said. One of the major conflicts dominating Trump’s second term as president will feature, but the other will not, the US officials said. “I think the president does intend to talk about Iran in the trilateral meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin,” a senior US official, speaking on condition of anonymity, told reporters on a call. Washington has a “whole other track” of negotiations with Kyiv and Moscow aimed at ending the war in Ukraine, the official added, referring to talks that US envoys have had in recent days with Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky. “China is not really a part of that track, so it doesn’t seem appropriate to have the Ukraine discussion there,” the official added. Tesla and Space X boss Elon Musk will accompany Trump on his trip to China but won’t be involved in the meeting with Xi and Putin, the officials said. Trump will also hold a bilateral working lunch and meeting with the Chinese president on Thursday — their fourth meeting since the US president’s return to power last year. But Trump is not scheduled to have a separate one-on-one with Putin. Among other topics, Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang’s resignation over an affair with an alleged Chinese spy is not expected to come up in Trump’s meetings with Xi, the officials said. “The situation with Nvidia should not really have any bearing on the trip,” a second US senior official said. The United States also did not plan to discuss export controls on sensitive chip technology, which were at the heart of the Nvidia scandal. “We do not negotiate American export controls. These are national security matters that we develop in the administration… and we don’t expect it to figure at all in any of our conversations with the Chinese while we’re there,” the second official said. Trump will leave Washington on Monday and arrive in the Philippines on Tuesday for a summit of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit before heading to Shenzhen. top.title: The King of Egypt! Mohamed Salah breaks national scoring record with ice-cold Panenka penalty
top.description: FBL-WC-2026-MATCH88-AUS-EGY - AFP Mohamed Salah has officially written his name into the history books as Egypt's all-time leading goalscorer. The 34-year-old forward netted twice late on in a dominant 5-0 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying victory over Malawi, sealing the milestone with a piece of outrageous audacity. Salah makes history in dominant Pharaohs win Salah has officially become Egypt's all-time leading goalscorer after netting a late brace against Malawi. The 34-year-old forward struck twice in the closing stages to inspire his nation to a commanding 5-0 victory . Salah entered the international break sitting just two goals shy of the long-standing national benchmark. By the time the final whistle blew, the veteran attacker had claimed the prestigious honour outright in front of an ecstatic crowd. Audacious Panenka seals landmark 70th strike The Trabzonspor star left it late to rewrite the record books during a frantic finale. Salah finally drew level with previous record-holder Hossam Hassan in the 84th minute, finding the back of the net to reach 69 international goals. Rather than settling for a share of the crown, the forward snatched the outright record in stoppage time. Awarded a penalty in added time, Salah showed remarkable composure to beat the goalkeeper with an audacious Panenka, securing his landmark 70th goal in style. Relentless form continues following Anfield departure Salah's latest milestone extends an international career that began back in 2011. Across 123 appearances for the Pharaohs, he has consistently delivered on the biggest stages while cementing his legacy as an icon of African football. His prolific touch remains intact at club level following his move to Turkey. Salah has already scored nine goals in 11 league appearances for Trabzonspor this campaign, becoming the first player since records began in 2014-15 to reach ten goal contributions across his opening seven Turkish Super Lig matches. Another major chapter in a legendary career Breaking Egypt's national scoring record adds to an extraordinary list of individual honours. Prior to his switch to Trabzonspor, Salah spent nine memorable years at Liverpool , departing Anfield as the club's all-time top scorer in the Premier League with 191 goals. During his spell in England, he also registered 277 goal contributions for the Reds - the highest tally by any player for a single club in Premier League history.

Wilkins sank the game-winner with 2.1 seconds left to salvage the hard-earned victory. The No. 24 Wildcats improved to 3-1, but the one-point escape against the unranked Lumberjacks could be a cause for concern. Especially if you ask Jamal Mashburn. Mashburn, who starred at Kentucky from 1990 to 1993, gave a blunt assessment of his alma mater on TNT Sports, as shared by SB Nation’s Chris Beasmore. There seems to be a lot of inconsistencies,” said Mashburn. “This is gonna be a long road, and I think a lot of people are gonna start asking the bigger question: What does Mark Pope ’s future look like? top.title: Done deal: Real Madrid midfield maestro has renewed his contract until 2031
top.description: Done deal: Real Madrid midfield maestro has renewed his contract until 2031 Real Madrid already have an excellent core of superstars at Jose Mourinho’s disposal, including Jude Bellingham. The youngest of them all, the Englishman is already performing at a very high level and still seems to have an even higher ceiling. At 23, he still has many years ahead of him, and according to Diario AS (h/t RMadrid actu ), Los Blancos have reached an agreement to extend his contract until 2031. The English midfielder is also set to receive improved financial terms that reflect his growth and status within the squad. Bellingham rewarded with new contract and salary increase The 23-year-old joined Los Blancos from Borussia Dortmund in the summer of 2023, signing a contract until 2029. However, both parties have agreed to add a couple of years to the deal. The salary increase is also warranted. Bellingham recently completed 150 appearances for Los Blancos. (Photo courtesy: Real Madrid official website) In fact, it is quite surprising that it has taken this long for Los Blancos to offer Bellingham a deal with better financial terms. For a player who played a starring role in his first season and helped the team win the Champions League, this deal should have come back then. Negotiations for the new contract are said to have begun towards the end of last season and are now nearing the finishing line. Bellingham has developed a strong connection with Madrid and its supporters during this period, recently surpassing 150 appearances for the club. Mourinho’s influence and Bellingham’s growing leadership Bellingham had a forgettable club season last year after persistent shoulder problems prevented him from performing at his best. Bellingham is already a superstar for club and country. (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images) However, he has returned to his best under Jose Mourinho this season, with the manager giving him the freedom to operate in attacking roles. His defensive commitment and willingness to lead Madrid’s pressing efforts have become equally valuable. Beyond his performances, the club also view Bellingham as a leader and someone who can fill the boots left behind by Luka Modric and Toni Kroos. A new deal is a show of faith from the Spanish club in the 23-year-old’s future, and it remains to be seen when it becomes official.

nigeria.title: Hundreds of million for 90 minutes, peanuts for a lifetime of service, by Stephanie Shaakaa
nigeria.description: *Nigeria’s Broken Scale of Value When the Super Falcons clinched their record-extending tenth Women’s Africa Cup of Nations title in July 2025, the Presidency rolled out the red carpet. The players received national honours, three-bedroom apartments in Abuja and the promise of the naira equivalent of $100,000 each. The financial rewards were eventually fulfilled in November 2026. Barely had that celebration settled when another Nigerian women’s team made history. The Flamingos conquered the world, becoming the first African country to win the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. Once again, the presidential purse swung open: ₦100 million for each player, secured in savings certificates because of their young age, ₦100 million in cash for the coach and ₦50 million for each member of the technical crew. The Senate also announced a separate ₦100 million reward. Let us be clear: nobody begrudges these young girls their glory. They trained hard, carried the green-and-white flag with pride and earned their moment in the sun. Their achievement deserves recognition, and the decision to preserve their rewards in savings instruments rather than hand enormous sums directly to teenagers is commendable. The problem is not that the government rewards sporting excellence. It is what the speed, scale and enthusiasm of these announcements reveal about the Nigerian state’s priorities. There is a disturbing arithmetic to our national life: hundreds of millions for 90 minutes of football, and peanuts, sometimes outright silence, for a lifetime of service. See the contrast in Abuja. When a trophy arrives at the Presidential Villa, the government can announce substantial financial commitments, organise receptions and put together carefully structured reward packages. Even the decision to protect the Flamingos’ money through savings certificates demonstrates an ability to think ahead and make financial arrangements in the interest of young beneficiaries. Yet, outside the celebratory atmosphere of the Villa, citizens encounter a different government, one that appears to require endless negotiations, industrial threats and public agitation before certain obligations receive the attention they deserve. The contrast extends beyond workers and pensioners. Consider the survivors of the Yelewata massacre in Benue State. Having lost family members, homes and livelihoods to violence, many displaced residents continue to struggle with food, healthcare, decent shelter and other basic necessities. Investigations into conditions in Benue’s displacement camps have documented irregular food distribution, inadequate sanitation, poor healthcare facilities and families struggling to secure even one proper meal a day. These are Nigerians whose lives have been shattered by violence. They are not asking for presidential honours or millions in savings certificates. nigeria.title: ‘I May Lose My Mind’, Frustrated Travellers React To US Flight Havoc
nigeria.description: Confusion reigned at airports across the United States on Friday as a rare grounding of all US flights stranded hundreds of thousands of frustrated travellers. In New York’s busy LaGuardia airport, Janice Llewellyn was on the verge of tears: the chaos could mean she will miss her daughter’s wedding in Toronto. The 61-year-old Llewellyn was desperate to find an alternative route, telling AFP: “I may lose my mind.” “My husband flew all the way from England to get to the wedding,” she said. “Oh gosh! I wish they had another flight, I wish I could get another flight, like, now.” At the airport in Las Vegas, some fliers were told their journeys were delayed due to wind. One airline staffer said the ground stop would last eight hours. Another said 24 hours. Passengers wait for updates at a check-in area at Terminal 7 at Los Angeles International Airport, in Los Angeles on November 13, 2026. US aviation regulators issued an extremely rare ground stop of all flights across the country on November 13 after a major communications outage, which the Department of Homeland Security said did not appear to be the result of any “nefarious attack.” Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) officials eventually lifted the ground stop at 8:15 pm ET (0115 GMT Saturday). “It will take us time (to) resume normal operations,” Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy said, blaming the incident on telecommunications issues with decades-old equipment. During the stop, the lack of information led many passengers to form long lines at rental car counters in a mad dash for travel alternatives. Joseph Anderson said he was trying to get back to Oakland in California from Las Vegas and was considering driving — but said “if the whole country is stopped, that means the highways are going to be jammed too.” The 72-year-old retired Air Force veteran said his already-checked luggage was captive, meaning “we’re kind of stuck.” “I would hope the communication can be better from the FAA,” he said. Passengers wait in line to retrieve their luggage as flights were cancelled at Chicago O’Hare International Airport in Chicago on November 13, 2026. nigeria.title: Trump, Xi, Putin to hold historic meeting in China – White House
nigeria.description: Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping will hold the first ever three-way meeting between the leaders of the United States, Russia and China at a summit in Shenzhen next week, the White House said Friday. Trump wants to talk about reducing nuclear arsenals at the trilateral talks on Thursday and is also set to bring up his war in Iran — but he is not expected to discuss Russia’s war in Ukraine, US officials said. The three leaders will meet on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in the southern Chinese city, White House spokeswoman Olivia Wales told reporters. “The president has made it clear that, among other topics, he will discuss the reduction of nuclear weapons in the world. This proliferation, President Trump believes, is very dangerous,” Wales said. One of the major conflicts dominating Trump’s second term as president will feature, but the other will not, the US officials said. “I think the president does intend to talk about Iran in the trilateral meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin,” a senior US official, speaking on condition of anonymity, told reporters on a call. Washington has a “whole other track” of negotiations with Kyiv and Moscow aimed at ending the war in Ukraine, the official added, referring to talks that US envoys have had in recent days with Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky. “China is not really a part of that track, so it doesn’t seem appropriate to have the Ukraine discussion there,” the official added. Tesla and Space X boss Elon Musk will accompany Trump on his trip to China but won’t be involved in the meeting with Xi and Putin, the officials said. Trump will also hold a bilateral working lunch and meeting with the Chinese president on Thursday — their fourth meeting since the US president’s return to power last year. But Trump is not scheduled to have a separate one-on-one with Putin. Among other topics, Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang’s resignation over an affair with an alleged Chinese spy is not expected to come up in Trump’s meetings with Xi, the officials said. “The situation with Nvidia should not really have any bearing on the trip,” a second US senior official said. The United States also did not plan to discuss export controls on sensitive chip technology, which were at the heart of the Nvidia scandal. “We do not negotiate American export controls. These are national security matters that we develop in the administration… and we don’t expect it to figure at all in any of our conversations with the Chinese while we’re there,” the second official said. Trump will leave Washington on Monday and arrive in the Philippines on Tuesday for a summit of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit before heading to Shenzhen. But some analysts doubt the discussions at the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons (CCW) will keep pace with the fast-changing weapons. AFP looks at three key questions ahead of the conference. What are LAWS? Lethal Autonomous Weapons Systems (LAWS) “can identify, select, and engage a target without the intervention of a human operator in the execution of these tasks,” said Jean-Marc Rickli, head of global and emerging risks at the Geneva Centre for Security Policy. Autonomous weapons have long existed. An anti-personnel mine “is an autonomous weapon in the sense that it explodes when someone steps on it,” said Laure de Roucy-Rochegonde of the Centre for Geopolitics of Technology at the French Institute of International Relations (IFRI). But with the proliferation of AI-enhanced drones, such weapons are now “capable of selecting and engaging a target that was not predetermined, adapting to their environment without human intervention,” said Rickli. nigeria.title: 6,000 Flight Cancelled: US air travel resumption will ‘take time’
nigeria.description: Flights in the United States were resuming on Saturday after being grounded for several hours due to a major communications outage, though authorities said returning to normal operations would take time. The nationwide stop on Friday sparked widespread chaos and left hundreds of thousands of passengers in limbo, with some pulled off planes moments before departure by airline staff who appeared in the dark about unfolding events. The incident marked only the second time such an alert had been issued in US airspace — which is among the busiest in the world — since the 9/11 attacks. The ground stop lasted around four hours and was lifted at 8:15 pm Eastern Time (0115 GMT Saturday). Federal Aviation Administration officials reopened the airspace on Friday night “after restoring full functionality” at air traffic control facilities, according to Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy. “It will take us time (to) resume normal operations… Our top priority is the safety of you and your family when you fly,” Duffy said. Administration officials blamed the incident on telecommunications issues with decades-old equipment, adding there was no evidence of foul play. “This is a legacy system problem,” Duffy said. “We have old, old switches, old routers. “We use 1980s little copper lines. It’s an old system that went down, and went down everywhere. It got overloaded.” Duffy had formally asked Congress on Thursday for $30.1 billion in funds to upgrade and modernize the air traffic control System. As the ground stop was lifted, he repeated his plea. “I’m going to say it a million times: the Congress has to give the resources to the president so he can finish this bill,” he said. 6,000 flights canceled There were almost 6,000 flights canceled, including some international routes, according to FlightAware, a tracking platform. Footage from airports around the country showed gates full, with planes waiting on taxiways. Passengers thronged concourses, desperate for information about an outage that had thrown their plans into chaos. “We’re trying to debate whether or not we need to reschedule or drive or what, but if the whole country is stopped, that means the highways are going to be jammed too,” said Joseph Anderson, 72, who was trying to fly from Las Vegas to Oakland, California. A nationwide ground stop is highly unusual. There was one such stop in January 2023 when a pilot notification system failed, but the only other national stop happened in the wake of the 9/11 attacks in September 2001, when no aircraft took to the skies for days. nigeria.title: Why 16 Nigerians died transiting through Addis Ababa
nigeria.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja The Federal Government has advised Nigerians, particularly those with underlying health conditions, to exercise caution when travelling through Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, following the death of 16 Nigerians in the city this year. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs issued the advisory on Friday, revealing that Nigeria’s diplomatic mission in Addis Ababa recorded 16 deaths involving Nigerians transiting through the Ethiopian capital. The deaths were reportedly linked to health complications associated with the city’s high altitude. According to the ministry, Addis Ababa is located about 2,355 metres (7,726 feet) above sea level, where lower atmospheric pressure results in reduced oxygen levels. The ministry noted that while most healthy individuals can adapt to such conditions, travellers with pre-existing cardiovascular or respiratory illnesses may face increased health risks. “This year, Nigeria’s Diplomatic Mission in Addis Ababa has recorded 16 deaths involving Nigerians transiting through the city, reportedly linked to health complications associated with high altitude,” the statement said. The government therefore urged Nigerians whose medical conditions could be worsened by high-altitude environments to seek medical advice before travelling through Addis Ababa. “Travellers with underlying medical conditions are strongly advised to obtain appropriate medical guidance before undertaking such journeys,” the ministry stated However, the Federal Government stressed that the advisory was not intended to discourage Nigerians from travelling to or transiting through Addis Ababa. “Rather, it aims to ensure that persons who may be medically vulnerable to the physiological effects of high altitudes are adequately informed and encouraged to take necessary precautions,” the statement added. The ministry reaffirmed the government’s commitment to safeguarding the health, safety and wellbeing of Nigerians abroad through timely travel advisories and other consular support measures. It is the kind of place where the weather decides more of the week than any calendar does, where a neighbour’s word carries the same weight as a document, and where the ground gives back exactly what the work put in. It is also where Egemen Mustafa Şener learned, before he ever ran a construction site in Istanbul or a shipyard project in Montevideo, the three practices that still organise his business today. The three words, as the company itself frames them, are labor, promises, and land. From a Black Sea farm to an Istanbul construction site Şener was born in Çifteköprü in May 1968. His father worked the land, his mother came from a well-established Laz family, and the household ran on a set of unspoken rules that any rural community would recognise. Work was visible or it hadn’t happened. A spoken commitment was binding. The land did not reward shortcuts. When he moved to Istanbul after high school, into business school and then into agricultural trading in the late 1980s, those rules didn’t get left behind. By the early 1990s, when he had shifted into residential and commercial construction and was managing his first sites in the city, the same three practices were doing the actual work of running the business. The language of the construction industry was new, but the habits underneath it were the same ones he had grown up with. Egemen Mustafa Şener on labor, in a sector where everything has to be seen The first of the three is labor, and in construction it is not a metaphor. A project is a stack of promises about what will happen on which date, and every one of those promises rests on someone actually doing the work. When labor becomes abstract, delivery slips. nigeria.title: Lumumba identifies what’s fueling xenophobia
nigeria.description: •Says Africa cannot fight poverty by turning against fellow Africans Professor Patrick Loch Otieno (PLO) Lumumba has warned that Africa’s failure to create sufficient economic opportunities is fuelling xenophobia. He urged governments to address unemployment, poverty and weak industrial development rather than blame migrants for the continent’s challenges. Lumumba, a renowned Kenyan legal scholar and public speaker, said xenophobia often thrived in societies experiencing economic hardship, where unemployment, inequality and pressure on public services encouraged citizens to regard foreigners as competitors. He spoke as the keynote speaker at the Bridge Club’s grand end-of-year event in Lagos on Thursday. In his address, titled Africa Must Not Become Foreign to Itself: Xenophobia, Pan-Africanism and the Future of African Belonging, Lumumba argued that migrants were frequently made scapegoats for economic problems arising from poor governance and weak institutions. He said: “The foreign trader, worker or entrepreneur can be arrested. The failure to create productive employment over several decades cannot be arrested at a roadblock.” According to him, African governments must look beyond the presence of migrants and examine the structural weaknesses responsible for unemployment, poverty and economic competition. He said the inability of many African countries to industrialise and create productive jobs had forced millions of young people into informal economic activities, where competition for limited opportunities could generate resentment. Lumumba observed that Africa’s economic dependence on exporting raw materials while importing finished products had contributed to the loss of employment opportunities to other economies. “We export crude oil and import refined petroleum. We export cocoa and import chocolate. We export minerals and import the machines, batteries and technologies manufactured from them,” he said. He added that the continent was effectively creating employment opportunities elsewhere while its young population continued to struggle for limited opportunities at home. The legal scholar said the appropriate response to the exploitation of migrant workers was to enforce labour laws against employers rather than encourage hostility towards foreigners. According to him, employers who engage undocumented migrants and pay them below lawful wages create resentment among local workers while benefiting from the division. “The appropriate response is not violence against the migrant. Adekoya spoke on Friday morning on The Morning Brief, a programme on Channels Television. He cited a calculation by Yiaga Africa. “If you look at Yiaga Africa’s calculation, 60 to 70% of voters are worried that political violence will not allow them come out on the day,” he said. He said that fear works against turnout. “Once the violence and the rhetoric of it goes up, people are less likely to come out to vote, and perhaps that is, some would argue, part of the strategy at play by some parties,” he said. There have been recent incidents, including attacks on party convoys and on an assembly in some states including Delta, Cross River, Lagos, Edo and Gombe states. In Delta State, a man was apprehended and not handed over to the police. He was then reportedly killed. Adekoya said violence was already rising and would get worse. “It is already ticking over 70 incidents captured so far,” he said. “This is not the peak of it because the campaign season has just started.” He said the stakes went beyond 2027, with politicians positioning for 2031 and 2039. “We expect that this political season will be a bit more violent and true to type,” he said. He said pressure on local politicians would raise tensions. “Politicians at the local level are under significant pressure to deliver on their areas and that would most likely raise tensions. What it will look like is that politicians use violence to destabilize the opponents in opponents’ area of strength so that they can lose votes.” Adekoya said his firm’s report classed 14 states as toss-up states, which would be “keenly contested”. He named the North Central, North East and North West, and parts of the South East, as areas of concern. “Nobody should die because somebody is trying to be president,” he said. On what security agencies could do, Adekoya said the shortfall lay in resources. “If at all there is a failure in security it is because of lack of capacity, poor logistics planning and the fact that we have a hydraheaded security problem which cannot be resolved,” he said. He said enforcement could not be left to the agencies alone. “There is a command structure where also politics get in the way of enforcement. It should not be a job only for the police, it should be a collective responsibility,” he said. nigeria.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The leadership crisis rocking the African Democratic Congress (ADC) took a decisive turn when Justice Peter Lifu of the Federal High Court, Abuja, invalidated the emergence of Senator David Mark and other executives who assumed control of the party in July 2025. But the judgment of November 5, 2026, was not simply about competing claims to party leadership. It hinged on a fundamental legal question: could the party’s National Executive Committee (NEC) use its constitutional powers to replace an existing elected leadership structure without complying with the democratic procedures prescribed by law? In the Certified True Copy (CTC) of the judgment obtained by Saturday Vanguard, Justice Lifu said he identified critical weaknesses in the defendants’ case, including the disputed resignation letter on which they relied, the limits of NEC’s administrative powers and the absence of satisfactory evidence that the new executives emerged through a democratic election. The resignation letter One of the Mark-led camp’s principal arguments was that Nafiu Bala Gombe had voluntarily resigned as Deputy National Chairman on May 17, 2025, before the NEC meeting that produced the new leadership. The letter, tendered as Exhibit ADC 1, was intended to establish that Gombe had relinquished his position and consequently lacked the legal standing to challenge the subsequent leadership transition. Justice Lifu, however, was unconvinced Rather than accept the document simply because it was certified, the judge examined its signature against Gombe’s signatures on other documents executed before a Commissioner for Oaths. He explained that certification established the status of a document as a true copy but did not, in itself, establish the authenticity of a disputed signature. After comparing the documents, he said that he found material differences in their structure, style, formation and general manner of execution. “The signatures do not appear to be one and the same,” Justice Lifu observed. He consequently described the purported resignation letter as fictitious or fabricated and rejected it as reliable evidence that Gombe had voluntarily vacated his office. The finding removed a central pillar of the defendants’ argument that Gombe had ceased to be an officer of the party before the July 2025 transition. Importantly, this was a finding made in determining the civil dispute, not a criminal conviction for forgery. NEC’s powers could not override the law The second major issue concerned the extent of NEC’s authority under Article 19(14) of the ADC constitution. Some patients who spoke to Weekend Trust said the rising cost of treatment had pushed them into financial hardship, forcing them to ration prescribed drugs, compromise their diets or go for days without medication. entertainment.description: “Oh my God, Uwaezu! You need to hear the latest gist!” My younger sister buzzed with excitement. Though we had been living in different countries for a couple of years, we still made time to talk every single week. Unfortunately, when she called, I couldn’t talk on the phone as I had been ambushed by my kids, who were brandishing their homework and threatening to cry if I didn’t help them. As a mom herself, she immediately understood why I couldn’t continue with the conversation. I quickly made my excuses, and we laughed and hung up, promising to catch up at a more convenient time. However, that exchange got me thinking about how most millennial women have a radically different marriage and motherhood timeline from our mothers. You see, when my mother was in her early 40s, my siblings and I were in university, so she had a lot of free time during the week to spend relaxing, hanging out with her friends, and attending social events. Basically living her best life. I, on the other hand, at 40-plus, spend my days cooking pot after pot of hot meals that immediately get devoured by my ever-hungry kids, teaching my nursery school-aged kids how to count and spell, and trying but often failing to enforce a strict bedtime with yelling and threats. I constantly feel myself going underwater and have to fight for my life every single day. There are other ways motherhood has been such a hugely different experience for me than it was for my mother. Like many women of her generation, she got married right after secondary school as university education was not seen as vital. This meant that she was a teenage mother and so had more energy to spare on her kids. She also benefited from having a lot of support from domestic staff and relatives. I do not have any village supporting me with child-rearing. I have hired domestic staff in the past, but it was always one thing or another, and they ended up leaving me stranded. entertainment.title: “Lagos Gave Me My Greatest Successes and Deepest Heartbreak”: DJ Cuppy Opens Up in Ifeoluwa Documentary
entertainment.description: Nigerian DJ and philanthropist Florence Otedola, popularly known as Cuppy, pictured wearing gold headphones and a camel-brown blazer. On her birthday, Florence Ifeoluwa Otedola is giving viewers a more personal glimpse into her life, exploring home, family, identity and purpose. For years, Nigerians have known Florence “Cuppy” Otedola as the internationally recognised DJ and philanthropist, often recognised by her signature pink hair and vibrant public personality. This birthday, however, her new documentary offers a closer look at the woman behind that familiar public image. Released on 11 November 2026, her new 12-minute documentary, Ifeoluwa , follows Cuppy back to Lagos, the city that shaped her and remains close to her heart. It is also a place connected to some of her greatest successes and deepest heartbreak. The title Ifeoluwa means “The Love of God”. Rather than marking the occasion with another glamorous birthday celebration, Cuppy has chosen to share a more reflective portrait of her life. The film explores womanhood, ambition, identity, belonging and the ongoing process of becoming. There are tender moments, too. Viewers see Cuppy not just as a public figure, but as a daughter, sister and granddaughter. Her time with her grandmother offers an especially intimate glimpse into the affection and family ties at the heart of her story. The documentary also captures an evolution audiences may already have noticed. Her signature pink hair has given way to a new look, while faith, education and service have become increasingly central to how Cuppy speaks about her future. This is not a rejection of music, but a fuller picture of the person behind it. Her philanthropic work remains an important part of that picture. Through the Cuppy Foundation, she has helped raise more than $17 million to support displaced children in Nigeria, in partnership with Save the Children. She has also established education funds at the University of Oxford, New York University and King’s College London to help students overcome financial barriers, particularly those from Africa. Alongside this work, Cuppy remains active as an international DJ, with performances at Glastonbury, Wireless Festival and Cannes Lions, as well as events during United Nations General Assembly week. The actress chose a bright fuchsia satin buba with wide half-sleeves, styling it with a fitted mini skirt made from emerald-green and magenta floral brocade damask . It’s an interesting way to rethink the familiar iro and bubacombination: keep the traditional top, swap the wrapper for a shorter skirt, and let the difference in fabric and colour give the outfit its character. The smooth finish of the pink satin against the patterned damask also shows how to wear two statement fabrics without making them compete . The trick is to give each piece a clear role, with the pink buba providing a bold block of colour and the brocade bringing in pattern and texture. sports.description: ROCKY RIVER — Grady Hirst ran for two touchdowns in the final 5:37 as West Branch (11-1) rallied for an impressive 21-12 win over previously unbeaten Rocky River (11-1) in a Division IV, Region 13 semifinal on the road. Gavin Marshall put an exclamation point on the victory with an interception on Rocky River's final drive that allowed West Branch to take a knee to run out the clock and advance. Barcelona faced financial obstacles despite Mikautadze’s interest Meanwhile, Mikautadze also talked about his readiness to take the next step in his career, despite recognising that he still has room to improve. “I’ve turned 26, but I think I’m ready to move to a big club. I have everything it takes, and I try to show that every time. Maybe I just need a little more time,” he said. sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino: why the newly appointed Man United manager will take this star to the stratosphere
sports.description: Mauricio Pochettino: why the newly appointed Man United manager will take this star to the stratosphere Manchester United have not made the best signings in recent years. Last summer was seen as an outlier, though, as all four players, Matheus Cunha , Bryan Mbeumo, Benjamin Sesko and Senne Lammens, all played key roles as United went from 15th to third in the league. This season has evidently been a disaster so far, as they sit 18th in the league in November, and Michael Carrick has paid for this start with his job. Matheus Cunha Whilst Cunha has not hit the heights of last season, he has still provided four goals and five assists in all competitions. This included a stunning brace to beat AS Roma in a magical night at Old Trafford in the Champions League earlier this month. Nonetheless, Cunha struggled under Carrick at times, playing as a number nine and being shunted out of his natural position to accommodate Marcus Rashford since his return this season. Mauricio Pochettino will love him Much has been made of incoming Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino’s admiration for Rashford , but he will arguably love Cunha’s profile more. Cunha will fit the Argentine’s tactics like a glove. According to Premier League analysis , Pochettino favours “a 4-2-3-1 system where wide attackers operate as roaming inside forwards rather than rigid touchline wingers. Starting on the left, Cunha can drift centrally into the pockets between midfield and defence while an overlapping full-back.” The Brazil international always looks more dangerous when he has licence to drift in and out and also drop into midfield, so this will be great news for him. In addition, players like Dele Alli and Cole Palmer, who like to operate in the half-spaces, have traditionally done well for Pochettino, so there is no reason to believe Cunha cannot also benefit. The former Tottenham Hotspur coach’s system also heavily relies on high pressing, and United are not a team full of natural pressers. Cunha, however, is great at pressing and harrying defenders into mistakes, and it seems natural that he would adapt well to Pochettino’s demands. What’s more, the head coach also likes to employ fast transitions in attack and, once again, Cunha has often hurt teams in England like this for Wolverhampton Wanderers and United. Finally, the head coach is renowned for his ability to man-manage and forge strong relationships with players. Therefore, he may just be the man to get the occasionally erratic Cunha to click, feel loved and stay on task. Featured image by Justin Setterfield via Getty Images online polls

sports.title: David Warner accuses Cricket Australia of ‘cover up’ over sandpaper scandal
sports.description: David Warner has sensationally accused Cricket Australia (CA) of executing a “cover-up” of the “sandpapergate” ball-tampering scandal in 2018. Warner, then vice-captain, was one of three players to serve long bans after a CA investigation into the use of sandpaper on the ball during the Test series against South Africa. Usman Khawaja had reopened the saga by writing in his autobiography that the whole Australian team were aware of the ball tampering, drawing support from close friend Warner and a strong denia l from now-skipper Pat Cummins . Warner, who retired from international cricket in January 2024, has now claimed that Cummins and the rest of the bowling attack – who have always denied wrongdoing – were not interviewed as part of the investigation. David Warner (left), Cameron Bancroft and Steve Smith all served bans for their role in the ball tampering scandal (Reuters) “As far as l am aware, CA did not interview Josh Hazlewood , Mitchell Starc or Nathan Lyon in their 2018 investigation," Warner said in a post on Instagram. "If that's correct, then how can CA push the idea that the bowlers didn't know? "It looks like they had decided who they wanted to blame from the very beginning, ran a shoddy investigation to serve the purpose and now they want to maintain the false narrative that the bowlers had no idea. That stinks of a cover-up." Cummins suggested on Friday that he had been talked to as part of enquiries in 2018. He, Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon have always maintained that they were unaware that sandpaper was brought on to the field in Cape Town to tamper with the ball. Australia captain Pat Cummins spoke to the media for more than an hour as he responded to Usman Khawaja’s claims (Reuters) Warner, captain Steve Smith and batter Cameron Bancfroft were the only players punished by Cricket Australia in 2018. Head coach Darren Lehmann was cleared of wrongdoing, though resigned his role at the end of that series. In response to the former opener’s new claim, a Cricket Australia statement said: “As we have stated previously, all players were given the opportunity to speak at the time of the initial investigation and have had the ability to come forward with new evidence in the eight years since. "Subsequently, CA has respected every player and former players' right to provide their own version of events." CA has previously said that it does not intend to reopen the investigation.

Salah makes history in dominant Pharaohs win Salah has officially become Egypt's all-time leading goalscorer after netting a late brace against Malawi. The 34-year-old forward struck twice in the closing stages to inspire his nation to a commanding 5-0 victory . Salah entered the international break sitting just two goals shy of the long-standing national benchmark. By the time the final whistle blew, the veteran attacker had claimed the prestigious honour outright in front of an ecstatic crowd. Audacious Panenka seals landmark 70th strike The Trabzonspor star left it late to rewrite the record books during a frantic finale. Salah finally drew level with previous record-holder Hossam Hassan in the 84th minute, finding the back of the net to reach 69 international goals. Rather than settling for a share of the crown, the forward snatched the outright record in stoppage time. Awarded a penalty in added time, Salah showed remarkable composure to beat the goalkeeper with an audacious Panenka, securing his landmark 70th goal in style. Relentless form continues following Anfield departure Salah's latest milestone extends an international career that began back in 2011. technology.title: Millions of Americans are not taking their GLP-1 drugs as prescribed
technology.description: GLP-1 medications are everywhere these days. The peptide-based drugs are both highly effective and wildly popular for diabetes, weight loss and a growing range of connected chronic health conditions, including cardiovascular disease and obstructive sleep apnea. But, amid the boom, the latest data suggests millions of Americans have turned to unapproved versions and are using the potent drugs in ways doctors never intended, raising questions about what that real-world use means for safety and efficacy. In a study published this week , researchers at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention broke down survey data of GLP-1 use collected between July and August of 2025. Based on responses from over 8,000 US adults, the researchers estimate that about one in 10 US adults (9.8 percent) used a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist, aka GLP-1 medication, in 2025. That's around 27 million adults. The study was published in the CDC's Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report. Among GLP-1 users, nearly half (44 percent) reported using their GLP-1 in a way that was different from how it was prescribed. Users skipped doses, delayed getting refills, and used smaller doses than prescribed, among other changes. More than half of the people modifying how they used the drug said the changes were because of cost or availability reasons. Cost and access barriers were most pronounced among younger GLP-1 users. Fifty-eight percent of adults 14­–39 years old who modified their use cited cost as a barrier, compared with just 20 percent of adults 65 or older who said the same. Read full article Comments

technology.description: Chalk up a new record for vulns. Microsoft alone added 1,094 security flaws to the total count on Tuesday, following 1,474 vulnerabilities the month before. “There's no denying the fact that vulnerability hunting with AI is driving a majority of what we're seeing.” All the major CVE Numbering Authorities (CNAs) - these are the organizations authorized by the CVE program to assign unique identifiers to security vulnerabilities - like VulnCheck, Microsoft, Oracle, GitHub, and other large enterprise IT vendors “are just screaming into the atmosphere right now,” Bressers said. “It’s AI.” Meanwhile, the percentage of these bugs that are exploited in the wild remains relatively consistent. About 1.4 percent (1,363) of the CVEs published this year have been added to VulnCheck’s Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog. “But obviously, as the number of CVEs grows, [1 percent] of 1,000 is a lot different than [1 percent] of 100,000,” Bressers said. technology.description: The internet is full of schlock, from biased news and dubious hot takes to false factoids. LogicLens aims to separate fact from fiction using the very same technology behind some of that slop: AI. It’s a simple premise, really: LogicLens, which lives in Chrome as a browser extension , or on iOS in the form of a mobile app called Receipts , combs through articles, social media posts, and other content to check it not only for factual inaccuracies, but also for bad reasoning. LogicLens and Receipts claim to identify logical fallacies , flag reports that misrepresent information, detect content that attempts to polarize an issue, and the like. It also cites sources, so if, for example, you need to call someone out on their BS, you’ll have ammunition. Or, if you’re trying to fact-check something before sharing it, you can get a more accurate view of the situation, and maybe post something else instead. Using the Chrome extension is as simple as clicking on its icon in the list of extensions in the browser. On iOS, the Receipts app is found as a share option. Once it starts, LogicLens scans an article, post, video, etc. to find potential issues of factual or logical inconsistency and flags them for review. If the facts of the matter turn out to contradict your worldview, LogicLens’ creators say they’re not trying to be partisan - you may just not be as informed as you need to be, which hopefully their tool will assist with. “We're not trying to be the referee of truth,” the company’s about page states. “Instead, LogicLens helps uncover the context, so you can decide for yourself without the spin." Of course, AI is increasingly used for online analysis and content review, and LogicLens is no exception. LogicLens doesn't identify the AI models powering its service in its publicly available documentation, but AI is definitely the backbone of the system. According to LogicLens, it's using an AI system that's “Research-backed and custom designed to outperform general models like ChatGPT & even trained experts.” We’ll leave that up to anyone willing to give the tool a spin to decide, but one thing’s for certain: The world needs something. technology.title: In elephants, the resilience of communities has its limits
technology.description: Elephants live in some of the most complex and resilient societies in the animal kingdom. Individuals die or move away, calves grow up, and newcomers join, but the local communities as a whole usually hold together. Long-term studies of African savanna elephants have shown that, even after poaching or other spikes in deaths, survivors tend to rebuild their lost connections over time. But a new study suggests that resilience may not keep the community intact when steady losses accumulate over time. Anastasia Madsen, a behavioral ecologist at the University of California, San Diego, and her colleagues analyzed 12 years of observations of wild Asian elephants in Sri Lanka. They found that, once losses began to outpace newcomers, the elephants’ society didn’t just get smaller. It fractured. Accidental savanna Udawalawe National Park in southern Sri Lanka was created in the 1970s around a reservoir on one of the country's four major rivers. “Before that, it was basically a tropical deciduous forest,” said Shermin de Silva, an ecologist at UC San Diego and senior author of the study (de Silva started the Udawalawe Elephant Research Project in 2006). science.title: New Scientist readers on how the magazine has shaped their lives
science.description: Have you been reading New Scientist since the start? Getty Images/Westend61 The first issue of New Scientist was published on 22 November 1956, and some of our readers have been with us since the very beginning. We asked subscribers, young and old, to tell us how they first encountered the magazine and how New Scientist has influenced their lives. The volume of responses and the gratitude expressed within them were quite overwhelming. Here are some of our favourites, featuring a spectacular maggot experiment, science-inspired poetry and even a match made on the short-lived New Scientist dating site. Huge thanks to everyone who wrote in. I was interested to see that New Scientist was launched “for all those men and women who are interested in scientific discovery and in its industrial, commercial and social consequences”. At the age of 13, I saved up a shilling from my Saturday morning “jobs” to purchase the first edition on 22 November 1956 and became one of those people interested in scientific discovery. Seventy years later, I remain a subscriber, after a scientific career that took me to many (if not, most!) countries in the world. New Scientist covered things like the opening of Jodrell Bank telescope in 1957. Since that was only about 50 miles (80 kilometres) away, it necessitated a bike ride to see what it really looked like! Peter Hall Advertisement I seem to have been reading New Scientist for the full 70! I do recall my encounter with the first edition: I was at Bec Grammar School in south London in a second-year physics class – it was 1956. The teacher, a genial boffin-type, announced the advent of the new publication and handed out copies – all I remember is its grey (or was it beige?) pages, which I read in a perfunctory way (I was only 12!) little thinking it would follow me through life and around the globe. Robyn Williams I was at Malvern College in England for my O level examinations from 1955 to 1958. My science master at Malvern had recognised my interest in science and technology and he bought the very first issue of New Scientist with his own money. At the next science class, he stood up in front of the whole class and waved the first issue, saying, “Young Inman, a new UK science and technology magazine has been published and here is the first issue for you.” I went on to reach 60 years as a member of the UK Institution of Civil Engineers. Peter Inman 1956 puts me back at school – Fettes College in Edinburgh. The school adopted New Scientist from its first edition and it was available in the library, where senior boys interested in science were recommended to read it. And so began a lifetime of New Scientist – I have been a regular for as long as I can remember and a subscriber for a very long time. I am very grateful to New Scientist for maintaining my interest in all the sciences and new developments, which I am sure has helped me to think laterally and to have a greater understanding of what makes everything tick.
